title: Rectangles and Squares
sourceStudentTask: Original 2021 requires FOUR separately produced drawing sets: FIVE rectangles, THREE non-rectangles, FIVE squares, THREE non-squares; pupils justify defining attributes of each.

teacherRubric.required: Five valid closed four-sided figures with four right angles; squares remain a subtype of rectangle. At least some size/orientation variety is considered.
The teacher validates defining geometric attributes, correct counts or decompositions, and a mathematical explanation consistent with the learner's own actual drawn/composed object.
The source requires a physical or drawn representation and verbal or recorded work. Naming a shape or number digitally is a partial assessment only.
The teacher can examine authentic learner-produced drawings or tracings only after these occur during learning; readiness of the rubric does not imply observed real student work.
Teacher checks three separately drawn non-rectangles and an explanation of missing four-right-angle attributes; five true rectangles must remain separately justified.

teacherRubric.criterion: Five source squares and three source non-squares
teacherRubric.required: Teacher examines FIVE separate valid closed four-equal-side/right-angle square drawings and THREE separate non-square drawings, with explanations. A non-square rectangle is a legitimate non-square but remains a rectangle. This is IN ADDITION TO the five rectangles and three non-rectangles.
